title: When Americans grew their own
dek: During World War II, home gardens grew a big share of the country's produce.
paragraphs: During World War II, the United States needed food for its troops and allies, and food rationing began at home. The government urged families to plant victory gardens.
Americans planted in backyards and vacant lots. Home gardens freed up farm crops, cans, and rail space for the war effort, and families canned what they couldn't eat fresh.
There were about 20 million victory gardens. They grew around 40 percent of the country's produce.
takeaway: Even a small garden stretches a pantry, and growing food is a skill that's far easier to learn before you need it.
